name: Bare Browser
statusNote: Bare 2.0 is in open beta on Google Play; v2.0.0-beta.1 released 27 Oct 2026
channels: Beta (Google Play open beta, GitHub pre-release)
updateCadence: Pinned Chromium revision, updated per release (196 patches in the series)
pitch: De-Googled Chromium for Android with full uBlock Origin and desktop extensions.
summary: A patch series on pinned Chromium that strips Google sign-in, telemetry, Firebase and Gemini/AI, keeps desktop extensions, ships full MV2 uBlock Origin, and adds background video playback and download handoff.
bestFor: Android users who want Chrome without Google, AI or telemetry
People who want uBlock Origin preinstalled
Users who want to hand downloads to 1DM-style managers
notFor: Users who want phishing/malware warnings (Safe Browsing is unavailable)
Devices older than Android 10 or x86

pros.title: Full MV2 uBlock Origin preinstalled
pros.detail: Bundled uBO is the full MV2 extension, works in incognito, and can be disabled or removed.

pros.title: Strips Google and AI
pros.detail: Removes Google sign-in, telemetry, Firebase registration and Gemini integration.

pros.title: Desktop extensions
pros.detail: Installs from the Chrome Web Store, CRX files or unpacked folders.

pros.title: Open-source patch series
pros.detail: BSD-3-Clause patches against one pinned Chromium revision, available on GitHub and Play.

pros.title: Media extras
pros.detail: Background playback with screen off, media saving, and a choice of download manager.

cons.title: No Safe Browsing
cons.detail: The README states no phishing or malware warnings in this build.

cons.title: Beta / small project
cons.detail: Tracks a single pinned Chromium revision and is still pre-release at 2.0.0-beta.1.

cons.title: No sync
cons.detail: Google sign-in is removed and no replacement sync was found.

cons.title: Clunky extension install
cons.detail: Android Police found Chrome Web Store navigation on a phone awkward.

signatureFeatures: Lockable incognito (biometric, wipe after failed unlocks)

faq.a: Yes, as org.barebrowser (Bare 2.0 open beta), plus GitHub releases; no account is needed.
Android 10 or later on arm64-v8a or armeabi-v7a; there is no x86 build.
Chromium component updater, uBO filter-list fetches and the GitHub build update check still make requests.

timeline.event: First alpha releases (1.0.0-alpha.2 RC3 added uBO in incognito)
Bare 2.0.0-beta.1 on Chromium 156.0.8078.25; open beta on Google Play

switching.note: Install Bitwarden etc. from the Chrome Web Store; no sync, so export/import bookmarks manually (unverified).

sync.note: Google sign-in removed; no sync documented

passwordManager.note: Use extensions such as Bitwarden (Android Police)

mv2.note: Full MV2 uBlock Origin bundled; desktop extensions supported

privacy.defaults: No Google sign-in, telemetry or AI; uBlock Origin on by default; DuckDuckGo search
privacy.telemetry: Browser telemetry removed; component updater and uBO list fetches remain

spec.telemetry: Removed; component updater, uBO list fetches and GitHub-build update check remain
spec.drm: Widevine may be provisioned via Google (README ambiguous)
spec.patchLag: Pinned Chromium revision: 156.0.8078.25 in 2.0.0-beta.1 (stable was 156.0.8078.73 elsewhere, small lag)
spec.languages: Chromium locales; translation via LibreTranslate-compatible server

notes: Google Play package org.barebrowser (open beta for Bare 2.0)
Android Police (Sep 2026) expected F-Droid later; not confirmed

privateHardening: Biometric incognito lock, wipe after failed unlocks, screenshot control
readerMode: Chromium reading/distilled page mode, availability varies
pip: Plus background playback with screen off
chromeWebStore: Install via Web Store, CRX or unpacked
pwaInstall: Add to Home screen; WebAPK needs Google services
devtools: Remote debugging from desktop; no on-device DevTools

jsSpeed: V8 on current Chromium, same JS speed class as Chrome for Android
pageLoad: Blink rendering gives Chrome-class page load on Android
networkSpeed: Chromium network stack with HTTP/3 and QUIC
startup: Full Chromium cold start; slower than WebView-based light browsers
smoothness: Chromium compositor gives smooth Android scrolling
memory: Multi-process Chromium footprint typical for Android
cpu: CPU use comparable to Chrome for Android
battery: Chromium battery profile similar to Chrome on Android
resourceControls: No tab-sleep or energy-saver UI beyond Android defaults
lowEnd: Chromium wants a modern 64-bit phone with ample RAM
installSize: Full Chromium build; large download vs light browsers
privacyDefaults: No Google sign-in/telemetry/AI; uBO on by default; DuckDuckGo search
blocking: Preinstalled full MV2 uBlock Origin, works in incognito
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox, but Safe Browsing removed
patchSpeed: Pinned Chromium 156.0.8078.25 on 27 Oct 2026; small lag behind stable
telemetry: Telemetry stripped; only updater and list fetches remain
behaviourCustom: Biometric incognito lock, screenshot control; few gestures
advancedSettings: chrome://flags available, no deep policy tooling on Android
tabManagement: Chromium Android tab grid and groups; no vertical tabs
searchFreedom: Chromium custom search engines, DuckDuckGo default
downloads: Download handoff to 1DM-style managers, media saving
productivity: Basics only: reading mode, PiP, no sidebar or notes
translation: LibreTranslate-compatible server option; Google Translate opt-in
extras: Background playback, media saver, incognito lock
extensions: Chrome Web Store, CRX, unpacked; full MV2
sync: No sync after Google sign-in removal
passwords: No built-in vault; rely on Bitwarden-style extensions
mobileApps: Android-only, Play beta + GitHub, arm only, Android 10+
devTools: Chromium DevTools via remote debugging from desktop
accessibility: Chromium Android accessibility, TalkBack and zoom support
businessTrust: Small project, transparent patches, no business model disclosed
longevity: New 2026 project, still beta, single pinned Chromium revision
beginnerFriendly: Extension install on phone is awkward; beta status
